stem: An analyst inherits the table main.ops.shipments and wants to know whether Databricks manages its files or whether they sit in a customer-owned location that other tools also write to. Which statement answers this from the SQL editor?

DESCRIBE TABLE EXTENDED main.ops.shipments, whose output shows the table Type (MANAGED or EXTERNAL) and its Location

stem: Delivery logs arrive as CSV files in an existing cloud folder that other non-Databricks tools also read. An analyst wants a Unity Catalog table over the folder without copying the data. Which statement type is appropriate, assuming the folder is a registered external location?

stem: A team has a curated sales table in Unity Catalog that only Databricks users read, and the analyst wants Databricks to handle file compaction, optimization and storage placement automatically. Which table type does this?

Managed table, because the platform owns its files and runs predictive optimization on them

stem: An analyst loads a Parquet folder into a Unity Catalog table to share inside the company, with no non-Databricks readers. Which choice is best?

stem: Yesterday an ETL job overwrote part of the table prices with wrong values. An analyst needs the rows that exist in prices today but did not exist at version 12, without changing the table. Which query does this?

stem: Finance needs the month-end revenue figure of every month to stay reproducible for two years. The source table uses default retention settings, and maintenance with VACUUM runs regularly. What should the analyst do at each month end?

stem: An analyst asks what Photon does for the dashboards and ad hoc queries that run on a SQL warehouse. Which description is correct?

stem: A team runs several kinds of queries on a SQL warehouse and asks which of them would gain the most from Photon. Which query workload fits best?

A stateful streaming query that keeps aggregates across micro-batches
A task that spends most of its time waiting for an external API to answer
A query that returns a single row in well under one second from a small lookup table

stem: An analyst creates a new SQL warehouse and asks whether Photon has to be switched on and whether queries need changes. What is the correct answer?

choices.text: Photon is on by default for SQL warehouses, and existing queries run unchanged
Photon must be enabled per query with a hint, and each query has to be rewritten in a Photon dialect
Photon is available only on classic all-purpose clusters, not on SQL warehouses of any type

stem: A query on a Photon-enabled warehouse uses one operation that Photon does not support. The query is slower than expected but returns results. What happened?

The query failed and was silently retried on a different warehouse type

stem: A team asks which of these workloads Photon is designed to accelerate. Which statement is correct?

choices.text: Queries written in Python, since SQL statements run on a separate engine that Photon leaves untouched
SQL, DataFrame API calls, ETL batch jobs and stateless streaming, without code changes
Stateful streaming aggregations, since SQL queries are already fast enough on the standard Spark engine
Machine learning model training on GPU instances, by offloading the gradient computation

stem: An analyst owns a Genie Agent for the sales team. A colleague should be able to add example SQL queries and edit instructions, but must not be able to change who has access or delete the agent. Which permission level on the Genie Agent fits?

choices.text: CAN MANAGE, because it is the only level that can change instructions and add example queries
CAN EDIT, because it covers instructions, sample questions and included tables but not permissions
CAN RUN, because it lets people ask questions and also edit the instructions that guide the answers
CAN VIEW, because it adds read access to instructions and lets the holder modify them in place

stem: A team lead shares a Genie Agent with the group "all account users" at CAN RUN. A finance employee opens it, asks a question and gets no data back, although the SQL warehouse is running. The employee has no grants on the finance schema. What is the correct fix?

choices.text: Grant the employee CAN USE on the agent's SQL warehouse, because the question needs warehouse permission first
Ask the agent author to share the author's own SELECT privileges by adding the employee to the agent
Raise the group's agent permission to CAN MANAGE, because CAN RUN does not allow queries on data
Grant the employee SELECT on the Unity Catalog tables used by the agent, because data access is checked per user

stem: A product team wants to show an existing Genie Agent inside its internal customer portal, so that portal users can ask data questions without opening Databricks. The author has CAN MANAGE on the agent. What else must be in place?

choices.text: The portal needs the agent's embedded warehouse credentials copied into its code so that the iframe can authenticate to the warehouse
A SQL alert must be attached to the agent, because the portal can only receive content that was pushed by an alert
A workspace admin has to configure the allowed embedding surfaces, and portal users need access to the agent and its data

stem: A company builds a scheduled backend service that sends questions to a Genie Agent through the Genie API. No person is present to sign in with a browser. Which setup follows the documented guidance?

choices.text: Share the agent with all account users at CAN MANAGE, then call the API without any credentials at all

Embed the agent as an iframe and let the service read the answers from the rendered page of the portal
Use the personal access token of the agent author for every call so that all users get the same answers

stem: A team keeps its Genie Agents together in one workspace folder and wants all agents in it to be usable by the support group without sharing each one separately. Which statement is true about how Genie Agents handle permissions?

choices.text: Agents sit in workspace folders and, like other workspace objects, inherit permissions from the enclosing folder

stem: Users of a Genie Agent click "Fix it" on many answers about fiscal quarters and add comments. The analyst expects the agent to behave better next week without any further work. What actually happens?

choices.text: Genie retrains itself nightly on the comments, so repeated feedback on one topic changes its answers automatically

Feedback is only visible to the user who gave it, so the agent owner can never see which answers were flagged

stem: An agent owner with CAN MANAGE wants to see which questions Genie answers badly and find recurring problem topics over time without reading every chat. Which approach fits?

choices.text: Export the SQL warehouse query history and count failed statements, because the agent keeps no record of its own conversations
Ask users to repeat each question in a new chat, then compare the answers by hand to decide which are wrong
Create a SQL alert on the agent's tables, because alerts report Genie answer quality to the owner on a schedule
Open the Monitor tab, filter by rating, and use Analyze Agent Usage to let Genie Code summarize recurring issues

stem: An analyst adds benchmark questions to a Genie Agent but leaves the SQL Answer field empty for most of them. After a run, the accuracy value is not shown and most rows are marked for review. Why?

choices.text: Benchmarks without SQL are skipped by the run, so they are removed from the list as soon as the run completes
Genie scores questions without SQL by comparing them to the text instructions, which takes a full week to finish
Only questions with a SQL Answer are scored automatically; the others need manual review before accuracy is reported

stem: An analyst designs benchmarks for a Genie Agent that answers revenue questions. Users phrase the same question in many ways. Which design follows Databricks recommendations?

choices.text: Several phrasings of the same question, each using the same SQL Answer, so wording variations are tested
One benchmark per question, because repeated questions inflate the accuracy value and hide real weaknesses
Only the most formal phrasing of each question, because informal wording is never expected from business users
One phrasing with a long evaluation note, because phrasing variations are checked by the SQL warehouse itself

stem: A benchmark expects a result with the columns region and total_revenue. Genie's generated SQL returns the same rows but adds a third column, avg_order_value. How does a Chat mode run rate this response?

choices.text: Bad, because a result set with extra columns compared to the SQL Answer does not count as a match

stem: In the Monitor tab an analyst sees that Genie answered a question about fiscal quarters wrongly. She edits the generated SQL, runs it and sees the right numbers. How can she make Genie answer similar questions correctly in future?

choices.text: Save the corrected query with Add as instruction so it becomes an example SQL query for similar questions
Copy the result as CSV and upload it to the agent, because Genie reads uploaded CSV files as its answer key

Click Regenerate response until the correct result appears, because Genie keeps the best of its past results

stem: A Genie Agent maps the word "Florida" to the stored value FL through entity matching on the state column. Last week the company added new state values and renamed some codes, and users now get empty answers for them. What should the analyst do?

Create a new warehouse, because stale values are cached in the compute that the agent uses for its queries

stem: A retailer's analytics model has one table of sales transactions with numeric measures and foreign keys, joined directly to flat tables for product, store, customer and date. Which data model is this?

A star schema, with a central fact table surrounded by denormalized dimension tables

A data vault, because the central table is linked to several descriptive tables by keys

stem: In a sales model, the product dimension was split into product, category and department tables, each linked to the next by a key, and the sales fact table links only to product. What is this design called, and what is the main trade-off?

choices.text: A snowflake schema; it removes repeated attribute values but needs more joins in queries
A data vault; it keeps history in satellites but cannot be queried by BI tools at all
A star schema; it removes repeated values but forces a full copy of the fact table per dimension

stem: A data team models its integration layer with tables named hub_customer (one row per business key), link_customer_order (relationships between keys) and sat_customer_details (descriptive attributes with load timestamps). Which modeling technique is this?

choices.text: A medallion layout, where hub, link and satellite are the names of the bronze, silver and gold layers
A snowflake schema, where link tables are the sub-dimensions of the customer dimension
A data vault, which splits business keys, relationships and history into hubs, links and satellites
A star schema, where hub tables hold measures and satellite tables hold the flat dimension rows

stem: While designing a star schema for orders, an analyst must decide where each column belongs. Which placement is correct?

stem: An analyst models a star schema in Unity Catalog and declares primary key and foreign key constraints between fact_sales and its dimension tables, although Databricks does not enforce them. What benefit do the declarations still give when the tables are added to a Genie Agent?

stem: Customer data comes from eight source systems whose attributes change often, and auditors need full history with the source of every record. Executives separately need fast dashboards on revenue by product and region. Which modeling choice fits both needs?

stem: A data analyst needs record-level, validated data for an in-depth investigation of individual customer transactions, which gold tables no longer contain because they are aggregated. Which layer fits best?

The team wants them to read the data without installing a second copy or contacting the provider. What should the analyst do?

choices.text: Ask the provider to add the teammates as recipients of the share, because only the provider can extend access to an installed catalog
Grant the teammates USE CATALOG, USE SCHEMA and SELECT on demo_census, because the requester owns the catalog of the installed product
Copy the tables into a team schema with CREATE TABLE AS SELECT, because a shared catalog is read-only and cannot be granted to others
Ask each teammate to request the same listing, because Marketplace data is licensed per user and each install is visible only to its requester

stem: An analyst owns the new table `retail.gold.store_kpis`, which has 45 undocumented columns, and colleagues struggle to understand it in Catalog Explorer search. She wants descriptions in place quickly but must not publish wrong definitions, and a Lakeflow job writes to the table every hour. A colleague who holds only BROWSE on the catalog must still be able to read the descriptions. Which approach fits?

choices.text: Generate AI-suggested comments in Catalog Explorer, review or edit each before saving, and save outside the hourly write since saving runs ALTER
Store each description as a tag value on its column, because tags are searchable and visible to users who hold only BROWSE on the catalog
Add the descriptions as Genie Agent column metadata, so they appear in Catalog Explorer and in search results for every workspace user
Turn on the catalog-level AI documentation setting, so that comments are generated and saved automatically for every column without review

stem: The governance team created the governed tag `data_domain` with the allowed values `finance`, `sales` and `hr`. An analyst who owns `ops.reporting.cost_centers` runs `ALTER TABLE ops.reporting.cost_centers SET TAGS ('data_domain' = 'finance')` and gets a permission error, while `SET TAGS ('project' = 'q4_review')` on the same table works. The value is spelled exactly as in the allowed list. Which change lets the analyst apply the governed tag?

choices.text: The analyst retries with the value written as 'Finance', because governed tag values are checked against the allowed list case-sensitively
A metastore admin grants the analyst APPLY TAG on the table, because table owners may set only ungoverned tags until it is granted explicitly
Someone with MANAGE on data_domain grants the analyst ASSIGN on that tag, since owning the table covers only the object-level tag right
An account admin grants the analyst CREATE on governed tags at account level, which is required before any governed tag can be assigned

stem: The STRING column `signup_dt` in `crm.raw.signups` holds dates from two source systems, written as `2026-03-14` or as `14/03/2026`, and a few rows contain junk such as `unknown`. The analyst needs a DATE column in a cleaned view. Junk must become NULL instead of failing the query, both valid layouts must parse, and the workspace runs with ANSI mode on. Which expression should the view use?

choices.text: `coalesce(to_date(signup_dt, 'yyyy-MM-dd'), to_date(signup_dt, 'dd/MM/yyyy'))`, which falls through to the second layout whenever the first one fails
`try_cast(signup_dt AS DATE)`, which detects either separator and layout by itself and returns NULL for any value that it cannot read at all
`to_date(nullif(signup_dt, 'unknown'), 'yyyy-MM-dd')`, which turns the junk value into NULL first and then converts all the remaining strings
`coalesce(try_to_date(signup_dt, 'yyyy-MM-dd'), try_to_date(signup_dt, 'dd/MM/yyyy'))`, keeping the first layout that parses and NULL when neither does

stem: A supplier shares the table `inventory_snapshot` with your company through Databricks-to-Databricks OpenSharing, and it appears in the catalog `supplier_share`. Ordinary SELECT queries work. To settle a disputed delivery, an analyst runs `SELECT * FROM supplier_share.ops.inventory_snapshot VERSION AS OF 120`, and the query fails, although the supplier confirms that version 120 still exists on its side. What explains the failure, and what fixes it?

choices.text: The table was added to the share without history, so the supplier must share it WITH HISTORY before recipients can run time travel
Version 120 is past the recipient's own seven-day retention window, so the analyst must raise deletedFileRetentionDuration on the table
The analyst lacks MODIFY on the shared catalog, which time travel needs because it reads older data files from the provider's storage
Recipients can never time travel on shared tables, so the supplier must export version 120 as a separate table and add it to the share

stem: Each month a store operations analyst receives a CSV of store codes such as `00731`, which she uploads into the volume `ops.raw.monthly_files`. She needs one Unity Catalog managed table, `ops.ref.stores`, replaced with each new month's file, and the codes must keep their leading zeros. She prefers the UI to writing SQL, holds CREATE TABLE on `ops.ref`, and has access to a running SQL warehouse. Which approach fits?

choices.text: Use Create table once on the volume folder as an external table, so every new monthly file is added automatically with STRING columns
Use Create table on the file in the volume, choose Overwrite existing table, and override the store_code column type to STRING in the preview
Use Create table with Create new table every month under a dated name, keeping the inferred types because inference keeps leading zeros
Use Create table with the default inferred types, then run ALTER TABLE to change store_code to STRING once the table has been created

stem: A data office wants Genie Code in every analyst's SQL editor to follow two conventions: use `finance.ref.fiscal_calendar` for any quarter logic, and always write three-level table names. Analysts should not have to configure anything themselves, and the conventions must keep applying when an analyst adds personal preferences that conflict with them. Only workspace admins may change shared settings. Which setup fits?

choices.text: The conventions are written as general instructions in a Genie Agent, which Genie Code reads whenever an analyst queries that agent's tables
Each analyst adds the conventions to her own .assistant_instructions.md file, which the data office then locks so that no analyst can edit it
The conventions are written as table comments on fiscal_calendar, which Genie Code treats as binding rules for every query it generates
A workspace admin writes the conventions into .assistant_workspace_instructions.md, which applies to all users and generally wins over user instructions

stem: A team runs everything on a classic SQL warehouse. It now wants a Genie Agent for sales managers and a Lakeflow Jobs dashboard task that refreshes a dashboard after each nightly load. Demand is bursty, idle in the evening with a rush at 9 a.m., and the team wants the LEAST sizing and scaling work with fast startup. Which warehouse choice fits?

choices.text: The existing classic warehouse with a larger cluster size and more maximum clusters, since Genie and dashboard tasks run on any type
A pro SQL warehouse with a minimum of one and a maximum of ten clusters, sized by the rule of one cluster for every ten concurrent queries
A serverless SQL warehouse, which supports Genie and dashboard tasks and lets Intelligent Workload Management add and remove clusters
A classic warehouse for the dashboard task and a separate pro warehouse for the Genie Agent, each set to the longest auto stop value

stem: A company will migrate from AWS Glue to Unity Catalog over the next year. Hundreds of Glue tables store Parquet data in S3, and analysts must join them now with Delta tables in Unity Catalog from Databricks SQL, without copying any data. The platform team wants the MOST cost-effective and performant read path and table-level governance in Unity Catalog. Which approach fits?

choices.text: Query federation over JDBC to the Glue Data Catalog, so the foreign catalog pushes each query down to Glue for execution on remote compute
Catalog federation with a Glue connection and an external location for the table paths, so foreign tables are read from S3 on Databricks compute
A Lakeflow Connect managed connector that ingests each Glue table into Delta tables incrementally, then retires the Glue tables later
OpenSharing from the Glue account to the Databricks account, so that each Glue table shows up as a read-only shared table in Unity Catalog

stem: The table `sales.silver.orders` gets a nightly MERGE that updates order statuses and deletes cancelled test orders. An analyst needs a dataset of daily revenue per region for a dashboard, refreshed after each load, with no hand-written reprocessing logic. A colleague proposes `CREATE STREAMING TABLE daily_rev AS SELECT ... FROM STREAM(sales.silver.orders) GROUP BY ...`. The totals must always match the current state of the source. Which choice is right?

choices.text: A materialized view grouped by day and region, because it recomputes correctly when source rows change, which a streaming read rejects
A dynamic view grouped by day and region, because it stores the aggregates and refreshes them whenever the nightly MERGE commits
A streaming table, because it processes each source row exactly once and so applies the nightly status updates to the totals by itself
A streaming table that ignores change commits in the source, so updates and deletions reach the daily totals without raising errors

stem: A logistics analyst reports delivery hours per region from `ops.deliveries`, which has about four billion rows and a long tail of very slow deliveries. The weekly dashboard needs an exact median per region and a 95th percentile per region, where a small approximation error is acceptable in exchange for lower memory use. Averages are not wanted because the tail distorts them. Which pair of aggregates fits?

choices.text: `percentile_approx(hours, array(0.5, 0.95))` as one array: an exact median and an estimated tail percentile in one call
`approx_percentile(hours, 0.5)` and `percentile(hours, 0.95)`: an estimated middle value and an exact tail value over every row
`avg(hours)` and `approx_percentile(hours, 0.95)`: the mean stands in for the median once the chart hides the slow tail
`median(hours)` and `approx_percentile(hours, 0.95)`: an exact middle value per group and an estimated tail percentile

stem: Finance reconciles two extracts of the same ledger, `erp_lines` and `dw_lines`, which have identical columns. Duplicate rows are legitimate: two identical 50.00 fees on one invoice are two real charges. The analyst needs every line in `erp_lines` without a matching counterpart in `dw_lines`, so that when ERP holds a fee three times and the warehouse holds it twice, exactly one copy is returned. Which query fits?

choices.text: `SELECT * FROM erp_lines INTERSECT ALL SELECT * FROM dw_lines`, which keeps each line as often as it occurs in both extracts
`SELECT * FROM erp_lines EXCEPT SELECT * FROM dw_lines`, the default set difference that compares both extracts row by row
`SELECT * FROM erp_lines EXCEPT ALL SELECT * FROM dw_lines`, where each warehouse row cancels one matching ERP row
`SELECT e.* FROM erp_lines e LEFT ANTI JOIN dw_lines d USING (invoice_id, fee_code, amount)`, keeping unmatched ERP lines

stem: A retention analyst lists customers by `last_order_date` so that the customers inactive the longest appear first in a win-back campaign export. Customers who never ordered have NULL in that column and must appear at the very end of the list, not at the top, and ties should be broken by `customer_id`. Which ORDER BY clause produces this order in Databricks SQL?

choices.text: `ORDER BY last_order_date DESC NULLS LAST, customer_id`, because descending order lists the oldest dates first with NULL values last
`ORDER BY last_order_date ASC NULLS LAST, customer_id`, because ascending order otherwise places NULL values before every date
`ORDER BY last_order_date ASC, customer_id`, because Databricks SQL always sorts NULL values after all non-NULL values by default
`ORDER BY coalesce(last_order_date, '1900-01-01') ASC, customer_id`, which replaces missing dates so that they sort to the end

stem: Shipment files arrive as CSV with a header row in the volume path `/Volumes/ops/raw/shipments/`. An analyst needs a Unity Catalog managed Delta table `ops.silver.shipments`, loaded once from all current files with column names taken from the header, so that Databricks manages its storage and predictive optimization can maintain it. No tool outside Databricks reads the table, and the files may be archived later. Which statement fits?

choices.text: An external CTAS, `CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE ops.silver.shipments AS SELECT * FROM read_files('/Volumes/ops/raw/shipments/', format => 'csv')`
A view, `CREATE VIEW ops.silver.shipments AS SELECT * FROM read_files('/Volumes/ops/raw/shipments/', format => 'csv', header => true)`
A CTAS, `CREATE TABLE ops.silver.shipments AS SELECT * FROM read_files('/Volumes/ops/raw/shipments/', format => 'csv', header => true)`
A table over the files, `CREATE TABLE ops.silver.shipments USING CSV OPTIONS (header 'true') LOCATION '/Volumes/ops/raw/shipments/'`

stem: After Tuesday's load, the Delta table `finance.gold.price_list` moved from version 41 to version 42, and a dashboard figure changed unexpectedly. The analyst needs only the rows that exist in version 42 but not in version 41, that is new or changed rows, in a single SQL query. The table must not be restored or copied, and change data feed is not enabled on it. Which query returns them?

choices.text: `SELECT * FROM finance.gold.price_list VERSION AS OF 42 EXCEPT SELECT * FROM finance.gold.price_list VERSION AS OF 41` as one query
`SELECT * FROM finance.gold.price_list@v41 EXCEPT SELECT * FROM finance.gold.price_list@v42`, which compares both versions in one query
`SELECT * FROM table_changes('finance.gold.price_list', 42)`, which lists each row that version 42 inserted or updated in the table
`RESTORE TABLE finance.gold.price_list TO VERSION AS OF 41`, followed by a query that compares the result with version 42

stem: An operations dashboard on a pro SQL warehouse runs about 40 small queries on each page load, and each one executes in well under a second. Users say the pages feel slow at 9 a.m. A manager proposes "turning on Photon" to speed things up. Query history shows that these queries spend most of their wall-clock time waiting before execution starts. What should the analyst tell the manager?

choices.text: Photon accelerates only notebooks on classic compute, so the dashboard should move to a notebook job that runs all 40 queries in one batch
Photon is already on, so the fix is a larger cluster size, because Photon speeds up each query in proportion to the memory per cluster
Photon must first be enabled in the warehouse settings, and once it is on, its vectorized engine also removes the queue time these queries show
Photon already runs on every SQL warehouse and adds little to sub-second queries; the waiting points to queuing, so raise the maximum clusters

stem: A query on the managed table `web.gold.events` filters with `WHERE CAST(event_ts AS STRING) LIKE '2026-10-%'`. It reads nearly every file, and the Performance insights tab shows `COVERAGE_STATS_DELTA` with the status Unused for that filter, although data skipping statistics are collected on `event_ts`. The analyst wants the same rows with far fewer bytes read, without changing the table layout. What should she change?

choices.text: Add a LIMIT clause and keep the cast, because the insight counts the rows returned to the client rather than the files that are scanned
Replace LIKE with ILIKE on the casted value, which lets the engine compare the text pattern with the statistics stored for each file
Rewrite the filter as a range on the raw column, event_ts >= '2026-10-01' AND event_ts < '2026-11-01', so file statistics can skip files
Run ANALYZE TABLE ... COMPUTE STATISTICS on event_ts, because the Unused status means that its minimum and maximum were never collected

stem: A report joins `fact_sales` (80 million rows) to `dim_customer` on `customer_id` and groups revenue by each customer's current segment. Totals look about three times too high, and the query profile flags `EXPLODING_JOIN`, meaning the join returns far more rows than it reads. `dim_customer` keeps type 2 history, with several rows per customer and an `is_current` flag. Which change fixes both the totals and the join?

choices.text: Switch to a LEFT OUTER JOIN, so every fact row is kept exactly once and the extra dimension rows are dropped from the result
Add AND d.is_current = true to the join condition, so that each sale matches exactly one dimension row for its customer
Wrap the measure in SUM(DISTINCT amount), so that rows repeated by the join are counted once while the join itself stays unchanged
Increase the warehouse size, since EXPLODING_JOIN means the join ran out of memory and the extra rows come from spilled data

stem: At version 57, a faulty `UPDATE` on `sales.gold.orders` set `discount = 0` for every order dated 2026-11-02. Versions 58 to 60 then appended valid new orders that must be kept. The analyst must put back the old discount values for the affected rows only, in a single SQL statement, without touching rows that the later versions added. Which statement fits?

choices.text: RESTORE TABLE sales.gold.orders TO VERSION AS OF 56, which reverts the faulty update and keeps rows appended by later versions
An UPDATE that sets discount from a subquery on VERSION AS OF 60, since the newest version still holds the discounts from before the error
RESTORE TABLE sales.gold.orders TO VERSION AS OF 57, because restoring to the version of a faulty write undoes that write's changes
A MERGE into sales.gold.orders with the table VERSION AS OF 56 as source, matching 2026-11-02 orders on order_id and setting discount

stem: The Unity Catalog managed table `logistics.gold.scans`, about 3 TB, has predictive optimization enabled, but a scheduled job still runs `OPTIMIZE logistics.gold.scans ZORDER BY (warehouse_id)` every night. Analysts' filters have shifted from `warehouse_id` to `carrier_id` and `scan_date`, and the team wants the file layout to follow the workload without maintaining a manual job or choosing columns again whenever query patterns change. Which change fits?

choices.text: Enable automatic liquid clustering with CLUSTER BY AUTO and drop the Z-order job, since predictive optimization never Z-orders files
Partition the table by scan_date and Z-order each partition by carrier_id, so that predictive optimization compacts every partition alone
Turn off predictive optimization on the table, because a table may keep either Z-ordered files or predictive optimization but never both
Keep the nightly job and let predictive optimization repeat the same Z-order columns, which it reads from the OPTIMIZE entries in history

stem: `daily_sales(sale_date DATE, revenue)` has one row per trading day, and stores close on some days, so those dates have no row. For each row the analyst wants the average revenue of the rows dated within the last seven calendar days, including the current day. Her query uses `avg(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY sale_date ROWS BETWEEN 6 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW)`, and around holidays the window reaches back more than a week. Which frame fixes it?

choices.text: `RANGE BETWEEN INTERVAL 6 DAYS PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW` with ORDER BY sale_date, bounding the frame by date values
`ROWS BETWEEN 6 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW` plus PARTITION BY sale_date, so each date has its own window and gaps stop mattering
`ROWS BETWEEN 7 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW`, which adds one row of headroom so each window covers a full week despite gaps
`RANGE BETWEEN 6 PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW` with ORDER BY sale_date, revenue, so that equal revenues stay inside the same range

stem: An AI/BI dashboard page has a Region filter widget and six charts built on the dataset `sales_ds`. A counter at the top must always show company-wide revenue, even when viewers filter the page by region or cross-filter by clicking bars, while the other charts keep responding to both. The author wants no duplicate dataset to maintain. What should the author configure?

choices.text: Turn the Region filter into a dataset parameter, because counters ignore parameters while field filters apply to every widget
Add a widget-level filter on the counter with Region set to All, which overrides the page filter widget and every cross-filter selection
Set the counter's Ignored filters to the page's Filter and Visualization sources, so it stops responding while other widgets still filter
Move the Region filter into the global filters panel, because global filters never apply to counter widgets on any dashboard page

stem: A dashboard dataset joins `fact_orders` (2 billion rows) with `dim_store`, and viewers pick one region from a field filter. Dataset queries are slow: the query profile shows the region filter applied after the join, and the insight `SELECTIVE_JOIN` reports that the join returns far fewer rows than it reads. The author wants viewers to keep the same region drop-down. Which change fits best?

choices.text: Keep the field filter but make it multi-select, because field filters on large datasets are always applied in the browser after loading
Add a :region parameter that filters dim_store inside the dataset query before the join, and connect the existing drop-down to it
Keep the field filter and add LIMIT 100000 to the dataset, so the result stays under the browser threshold and filtering runs locally
Replace the field filter with widget-level filters on each chart, because widget filters are pushed into the join of the dataset query

stem: The owner of an AI/BI dashboard published it with shared data permissions, and managers without table access view it without errors. A new co-author receives CAN EDIT, opens the draft to add a chart, and every widget fails with a permission error on `finance.gold.margin`, a table on which the co-author has no grants. The published version still works for the managers. Which explanation is correct?

choices.text: Shared data permissions apply only to account users outside the workspace, so workspace members always need their own table grants
CAN EDIT carries no data access, so the owner must also grant CAN RUN, which makes the draft use the embedded publisher credential
The shared credential applies to the draft only after the co-author republishes, so the co-author should publish first and then edit
Drafts always run with the viewer's own data permissions, so the co-author needs SELECT and usage privileges to work in the draft

stem: An analyst must send a weekly PDF of the EMEA view of a published dashboard to an external auditor who has no Databricks account, and to the internal finance group. Other viewers keep the default of All regions, and the scheduled refresh should run on a separate small warehouse so it does not compete with daytime users. Which configuration fits?

choices.text: A dashboard task in a job, with the auditor shared on the dashboard at CAN VIEW, since view access mails the PDF to every viewer weekly
A SQL alert on the EMEA dataset that emails the auditor each week and attaches the dashboard as a PDF through its notification template
A schedule with default filters, the auditor typed in as a workspace user's email address, and the warehouse switched in the Data tab
A schedule that applies the current EMEA filter selection and its own warehouse, with an admin-made email destination for the auditor

stem: An alert query lists sites with more than 20 failed loads today: `SELECT site, count(*) AS failed FROM ops.loads WHERE status = 'FAILED' AND load_date = current_date() GROUP BY site HAVING count(*) > 20`. On good days it returns no rows. The on-call team wants the alert to evaluate to OK on those days, and they also want a message when the alert recovers after having fired. Which settings fit?

choices.text: In Advanced settings set Empty result state to Triggered and turn on Notify on OK, so each quiet day is flagged and recoveries are sent
In Advanced settings set Empty result state to OK and turn on Notify on OK, with the condition failed greater than 20 on the result
Keep the defaults, because an empty result evaluates to OK unless configured, and the alert then also reports each recovery by itself
Change the query to return raw rows without GROUP BY, because an alert condition can be checked only on rows that are not aggregated

stem: An executive page must show, per month over the last two years, revenue in millions and gross margin as a percentage, so leaders can see whether margin fell in months when revenue rose. The two measures have very different scales, and the author wants one chart that shares the month axis rather than two charts placed side by side. Which visualization fits?

choices.text: A scatter chart with revenue on the X axis and margin on the Y axis and one point per month, which shows how the two measures relate
A pie chart for every month with revenue and margin as slices, so the share of each measure is visible within every single month
A combo chart with a bar layer for revenue and a line layer for margin, with dual axis turned on so each measure has its own Y axis
A stacked bar chart with revenue and margin as two series, so both values appear inside each month's bar against the same Y axis

stem: A Genie Agent for sales has the tables `orders` and `customers` attached as sources. Its general instructions say "use `finance.gold.fx_rates` to convert all amounts to EUR", and the analyst confirmed that every user of the agent has SELECT on that table. Yet Genie never converts amounts and never references fx_rates in its generated SQL. What is the cause, and what is the fix?

choices.text: Genie queries only sources attached to the agent, whatever instructions say; attach fx_rates as a source and keep the instruction
Genie ignores instructions that name tables in other catalogs, so fx_rates should be moved into the same schema as orders
Text instructions need a parameterized example query before they activate, so until one exists Genie treats them as background
Instructions take effect only after users click Fix it on an answer, so users should flag one answer to start the conversions

stem: A Genie Agent's answers join `opportunity` to `accounts` on the wrong column and double-count deals. No primary or foreign key constraints exist in Unity Catalog, and the analyst who curates the agent has CAN EDIT on it but cannot alter the underlying tables, which belong to the CRM team. The fix must take effect for this agent today. Which change should the analyst make first?

choices.text: Define a many-to-one join relationship from opportunity to accounts in the knowledge store, with accounts.id = opportunity.accountid
Write a general instruction that lists all 40 columns of both tables, which Genie applies to every prompt as the binding join definition
Hide every column of accounts except id, so that Genie has no other column it could pick when it joins the two tables together
Add PRIMARY KEY and FOREIGN KEY constraints to both tables, which Genie then saves as join relationships during knowledge mining

stem: A Genie Agent has served 300 business users for months. This morning every question fails with a warehouse access error, for all users at once. No Unity Catalog grants changed, and the warehouse is running. The analyst who last configured the agent's default warehouse left the company yesterday and was removed from the workspace. What restores the agent for everyone?

choices.text: A workspace admin grants CAN USE on the warehouse to all 300 users, because Genie now runs each query with the user's own compute access
Another user with at least CAN EDIT on the agent reselects and saves the default warehouse, which embeds that user's compute credentials
An admin clones the agent, because an agent whose author was removed can no longer be edited and its monitoring data is lost anyway
A metastore admin transfers ownership of every table used by the agent to a service principal, so the queries no longer depend on a person

stem: A benchmark question in a Genie Agent asks for "all orders shipped late in October", and its SQL Answer returns about 12,000 rows without an ORDER BY clause. The analyst compares Genie's generated SQL by hand and finds it equivalent, yet every Chat mode run rates the question Bad, while the other benchmarks of the agent pass. What is the most likely cause, and what fixes it?

choices.text: Benchmarks rate any question with more than 10,000 result rows as Bad by design, so the question must be removed from the benchmark set
Genie returns the same rows in another order, and Chat mode always rates a result set as Bad when its rows are sorted differently
Chat mode compares only the first 5,000 rows, so a different row order compares different rows; add ORDER BY to both or return fewer rows
The SQL Answer must come from the Generate SQL button, because handwritten answers are compared by query text rather than by results

stem: A Genie Agent built on six wide tables, about 400 columns in total, shows a token limit warning, and its answers have become slower and less precise. Most users ask about only 30 of those columns. The curator cannot change the source tables, and other teams query those tables directly with all their columns. What should the curator do first?

choices.text: Revoke SELECT on the unused columns from the agent's users, because Genie counts only the columns that each asking user may read
Add example SQL queries that cover every one of the 400 columns, so that Genie needs fewer tokens to reason about rare columns
Split the agent into six agents with one table each, because the token limit applies per table and each agent then stays under it
Hide unneeded columns in the agent and trim redundant column descriptions, shrinking Genie's context without changing the tables

stem: The fact table `fact_orders` holds `order_date_key` and `ship_date_key`, both pointing to the single dimension `dim_date`, which has one row per day with fiscal week and a holiday flag. A report must show, per order, the fiscal week in which it was ordered and the fiscal week in which it shipped, side by side. The model must stay a star schema with no new tables. Which query pattern fits?

choices.text: Join dim_date twice under two aliases, once on order_date_key and once on ship_date_key, and select the fiscal week from each alias
Create dim_ship_date as a physical copy of dim_date, because a star schema allows each dimension to join a fact table only once
Join dim_date once on order_date_key OR ship_date_key, so a single join brings in the fiscal week of both dates for every order
Copy both fiscal weeks into fact_orders as columns, because star schemas keep descriptive attributes on the fact table to avoid joins

stem: `dim_product` is a type 2 slowly changing dimension with `product_id`, `category`, `valid_from` and `valid_to`, where the current row has `valid_to = '9999-12-31'`. Products sometimes move between categories during the year. Finance needs 2025 revenue grouped by the category each product belonged to on the day of the sale, not by its current category, and each sale must be counted once. Which join from `fact_sales` gives this?

choices.text: Join on product_id and group by both category and valid_from, so each version's revenue is a separate row to add up later
Join on product_id only and keep the version with the latest valid_from for each sale, so every sale uses its newest category
Join on product_id with sale_date >= valid_from AND sale_date < valid_to, so each sale matches the version valid on that day
Join on product_id where valid_to = '9999-12-31', so that every sale matches exactly one dimension row without duplicates

stem: Analysts in the development workspace must query the production catalog `prod_sales` for testing, but no user or job in that workspace may ever write to it, including principals who hold MODIFY there for their production work. The production workspace must keep full read and write access. Both workspaces are attached to the same metastore, and the team wants one setting rather than per-table work. Which setting fits?

choices.text: Bind prod_sales only to the production workspace, so development users still see it read-only through the default behavior
Revoke MODIFY on prod_sales from all groups, then grant it back only within the production workspace as a workspace-level grant
Create a dynamic view over each table for development users, because views are read-only while the source catalog stays writable
Bind prod_sales to both workspaces and set the development workspace binding to read-only, so every write from it is blocked

stem: A migration script created a catalog named `emea-sales`. An analyst runs `SELECT * FROM emea-sales.crm.accounts` in the SQL editor and gets a parse error, although she holds SELECT and the usage privileges and can see the table in Catalog Explorer. Nothing may be renamed because other jobs reference the catalog by that name, and the query must stay a single statement. Which query works?

choices.text: SELECT * FROM "emea-sales".crm.accounts, because double quotes are the standard way to delimit identifiers in Databricks SQL
SELECT * FROM `emea-sales`.crm.accounts, delimiting the catalog name with backticks because it contains a hyphen
SELECT * FROM crm.accounts after running USE CATALOG emea-sales, since USE statements accept special characters unquoted
SELECT * FROM emea_sales.crm.accounts, because Unity Catalog stores hyphens as underscores and accepts both spellings

stem: Analysts must count distinct customers and join `crm.core.customers` to `web.gold.sessions` on the email column, but only the privacy team may see real addresses. Many dashboards query both tables directly, and the solution must not force anyone to switch to new object names. The privacy team also wants one control that is enforced wherever the tables are queried. Which control fits?

choices.text: Dynamic views over both tables that hide the email column for non-members, with every dashboard moved over to the new views
Removing SELECT on the email column from the analysts group, so analysts can still query every other column of both tables
A column mask on email in both tables that returns 'REDACTED' to everyone outside the privacy group, so no address is ever seen
A column mask on email in both tables that returns the address to the privacy group and sha2(email, 256) to everyone else

stem: The metric view `sales.semantic.revenue_mv` feeds a busy executive dashboard. To speed it up, the analyst adds a `materialization` block with an aggregated materialized view by month and region and a six-hour schedule, but the change is rejected. The serverless setting is on and the SQL warehouse runs a current version. While checking the sources, she notices that `sales.gold.orders`, one of the joined tables, has had a row filter since last quarter so that country managers see only their own countries, and the dashboard is published with individual data permissions. Query profiles of the dashboard never show `METRIC_VIEW_MATERIALIZATION_MATCH`. What explains this, and what is the right next step?

choices.text: Materialization needs an unaggregated materialized view when a source has a row filter, because filters apply to rows; replace the aggregated one
Materialization is unavailable while the dashboard uses individual permissions, because each viewer needs a cache; publish with shared permissions
Materialization is unavailable while a source uses a row filter, because it is computed once as the owner; keep live queries and tune the sources
Materialization needs the schedule removed when a source has a row filter, because each refresh must run as the viewer; refresh it manually instead

stem: A pricing analyst can browse Databricks Marketplace and open listing pages, but clicking Get instant access on a free listing fails with a permission error. An admin explains that `USE MARKETPLACE ASSETS` was revoked from all users last year under a data intake policy, and that the policy stays in place; analysts who may install listings receive the narrowest alternative rights. The analyst already holds `CREATE CATALOG` on the metastore for a sandbox project and must not become a metastore admin. The installed data must land as a catalog that she can then share with her team. Which additional grant lets her install the listing?

choices.text: CREATE SHARE on the metastore, which together with her existing CREATE CATALOG is the documented alternative to USE MARKETPLACE ASSETS
USE PROVIDER on the metastore, which together with her existing CREATE CATALOG is the documented alternative to USE MARKETPLACE ASSETS
USE RECIPIENT on the metastore, which together with her existing CREATE CATALOG is the documented alternative to USE MARKETPLACE ASSETS
CREATE PROVIDER on the metastore, which together with her existing CREATE CATALOG is the documented alternative to USE MARKETPLACE ASSETS

stem: For two years analysts tagged their own tables with a free-form tag `owner_team`, using values such as `fin`, `finance` and `Finance-EMEA`. Last week the governance team created an account-level governed tag with the same key `owner_team` and the allowed values `finance`, `sales` and `hr`, and granted ASSIGN on it only to data stewards. Today an analyst who owns `fin.reporting.budget` tries to change its tag from `fin` to the allowed value `finance` and gets a permission error, although the same change worked last month and she can still add other free tags to the table. What explains this?

choices.text: Existing owner_team assignments became governed when the tag was created, so changing them now needs ASSIGN, which only stewards hold
Existing owner_team assignments stay free tags until a steward converts them, so the error comes from a missing APPLY TAG on her table
Existing owner_team assignments became governed when the tag was created, so the old value fin must be in the allowed list before any change
Existing owner_team assignments were deleted when the tag was created, so the analyst must first recreate the old value fin before changing it

stem: An analyst cleans duplicate imports in `crm.raw.contacts` with a view: `SELECT * FROM crm.raw.contacts QUALIFY row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY contact_id ORDER BY imported_at DESC) = 1`. Reconciliation shows that for about 2% of contacts the kept phone number changes from one run to the next, although the source table did not change. Inspecting those contacts, she finds two rows with the same `imported_at` second from a batch loader, differing in `phone` and in `source_file`, which holds names such as `batch_0412.csv` that increase with load order. The rule is "keep the row from the latest file". Which change makes the view deterministic and correct?

choices.text: Replace row_number() with rank() under the same ORDER BY, so that tied rows on the timestamp receive the same rank and are both kept
Replace row_number() with dense_rank() under the same ORDER BY, so that tied rows share a rank and the next one follows without a gap
Order the window by imported_at DESC, phone DESC, so that ties on the timestamp are broken by the phone number in a fixed order every time
Order the window by imported_at DESC, source_file DESC, so that ties on the timestamp are broken by the later file name every time

stem: Analysts query a busy SQL Server order database through a foreign catalog. Five dashboards refresh every 15 minutes and each refresh reads several million rows, and the database team reports that these federated reads now slow the order application at peak hours. The business needs order data in Databricks no more than 15 minutes old, at higher volumes next year, with joins to Delta tables. The database team has agreed to enable change tracking on the source tables and wants to stop the repeated full reads. Which approach fits BEST?

choices.text: Catalog federation to the SQL Server catalog, so queries read the database files directly from object storage using Databricks compute only
A Lakeflow Connect SQL Server connector that ingests the tables incrementally into Unity Catalog through change tracking on a 15-minute schedule
Query federation kept with a larger JDBC fetchSize on each dashboard query, so every refresh pulls the same rows in fewer network round trips
A materialized view over each foreign table refreshed every 15 minutes, so dashboards read Delta while each refresh still reads the source in full

stem: An auditor asks for the contents of the Unity Catalog managed table `finance.gold.accruals` as of 12 days ago. `DESCRIBE HISTORY` lists versions going back about four weeks, and the analyst picks version 318 from 12 days ago, but `SELECT * FROM finance.gold.accruals VERSION AS OF 318` fails with an error saying the version is outside the retention window. Nobody has run VACUUM manually, the table properties show no custom retention settings, and the query runs on a current serverless SQL warehouse. Future audits will need 60 days. Which explanation and change are right?

choices.text: Time travel is blocked past logRetentionDuration (30 days by default) on managed tables; raise it to 60 days and keep the file retention as it is
Time travel is blocked only after a manual VACUUM on managed tables; tell the team never to run VACUUM so that 60 days of versions stay readable
Time travel stops at deletedFileRetentionDuration (7 days by default) on managed tables; raise it and logRetentionDuration to 60 days
Time travel is blocked past deletedFileRetentionDuration (7 days by default) on managed tables; raise only that property to 60 days for audits

stem: The source table `pos.silver.transactions` is a date-partitioned Delta table, and a compliance job deletes rows older than 400 days every night. Finance wants a table of yearly revenue per store that keeps the totals for every past year forever, refreshed daily. An analyst built it as a materialized view on a serverless SQL warehouse: `CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW fin.gold.yearly_rev SCHEDULE EVERY 1 DAY AS SELECT store_id, year(ts) AS yr, sum(amount) AS rev FROM pos.silver.transactions GROUP BY ALL`. Two months after go-live, the totals for the oldest year began shrinking, while the refresh history shows only successful incremental refreshes. Which change meets the requirement?

choices.text: Build the yearly totals from a streaming table that reads new source rows once, so later deletions in the source leave the stored totals in place
Keep the materialized view and enable row tracking on the source table, so that incremental refreshes ignore rows removed by the deletion job
Keep the materialized view and switch its refresh to FULL each night, so that the yearly totals are recomputed from every row on each run
Keep the materialized view and add TRIGGER ON UPDATE to it, so that the totals are refreshed before each nightly deletion job removes any rows

stem: A dashboard dataset reads the MySQL table `ops_fed.crm.tickets` (40 million rows, six years of history) through query federation with `SELECT ticket_id, subject, created_at FROM ops_fed.crm.tickets WHERE subject ILIKE '%refund%'`. Each refresh takes minutes. `EXPLAIN FORMATTED` shows that the query sent to MySQL has no WHERE clause, so all rows travel to Databricks. The only chart on the page shows refund tickets from the last 30 days, trimmed by a date setting inside the chart. MySQL cannot be changed, and the dashboard must keep showing the same tickets. Which change reduces the rows fetched over the network?

choices.text: Add AND created_at >= :start_date to the dataset query, so the pushable date predicate reaches MySQL while ILIKE runs on Databricks
Set a larger fetchSize on the dataset query, so the warehouse reads the full table in fewer round trips and filters it locally as before
Build a materialized view over the foreign table refreshed hourly, so the dashboard reads Delta while each refresh fetches the same rows
Change the dataset to OR created_at >= :start_date, so MySQL evaluates the date predicate while Databricks evaluates the ILIKE part

stem: A slow dashboard query on `retail.gold.sales` (a Unity Catalog managed table) shows two insights in its query profile: `WIDE_PROJECTION`, because the dataset uses `SELECT *` while the charts need six columns, and `DATA_FILE_SIZE`, because the scan reads tens of thousands of small files. The analyst selects Optimize, which opens Genie Code. She expects Genie Code to fix both problems in one step, but it presents a rewritten query for approval and only a plain-language note about the files. She has SELECT on the table and no MODIFY. What explains this, and what should she do?

choices.text: Genie Code rewrites both kinds of insight but only in the SQL editor, not from the profile; reopen the query there and run Optimize again
Genie Code rewrites both kinds of insight but needs MODIFY to show the table change; ask for MODIFY and run Optimize again on the query
Genie Code rewrites only query-level insights and describes table or compute insights as text; accept the rewrite and pass the file note to the owner
Genie Code rewrites only query-level insights and describes table or compute insights as text; accept the rewrite and run OPTIMIZE herself

stem: The managed table `web.gold.clicks` (8 TB) uses liquid clustering with `CLUSTER BY (event_date)`, where `event_date` is a DATE column filled from the TIMESTAMP column `event_ts` at load time. A dashboard dataset filters `WHERE event_ts >= :start_ts AND event_ts < :end_ts` for one-day windows, and the profile shows almost no files pruned and the insight `COVERAGE_FILTER_KEYS_CLUSTERING`. Statistics are complete, and other dashboards on the table filter by `event_date` and run fast. About 200 store managers open the dashboard every morning. The analyst may change only the dataset query, not the table or its clustering keys. Which change fits?

choices.text: Replace the timestamp range with CAST(event_ts AS DATE) = to_date(:start_ts), so the scan compares one day just like the key column
Keep the timestamp range and add AND event_date BETWEEN to_date(:start_ts) AND to_date(:end_ts), so the scan filters on the clustering key
Keep the timestamp range and add ORDER BY event_date to the dataset, so the scan reads the files in clustering key order and skips more
Keep the timestamp range and add AND to_date(event_ts) BETWEEN to_date(:start_ts) AND to_date(:end_ts), so the scan filters by day

stem: A colleague asks an analyst to share the query profile of a report query that "suddenly became instant". In query history, the latest run shows a duration of a few milliseconds and the message "Query profile is not available" when she clicks See query profile. Earlier runs of the same text last week have profiles, and a teammate ran the identical text two hours earlier. The source tables have not changed since then, the warehouse is serverless, and the colleague wants to study the full execution, not the cached result. What explains the missing profile, and how can the analyst get one?

choices.text: The run was answered from the disk cache, which yields no profile; restart the serverless warehouse so that the disk cache is emptied first
The run was answered from the query result cache, which yields no profile; wait 7 days until the cache entry for the query expires
The run was answered from the dashboard cache, which yields no profile; open the query from the dashboard so that the warehouse rescans data
The run was answered from the query result cache, which yields no profile; rerun with a trivial change to the text such as the LIMIT

stem: The table `mkt.ext.campaign_events` is an external Delta table, because an outside marketing tool writes files to its location every hour, and it must stay external. Predictive optimization is enabled for the whole account. Join-heavy dashboard queries on it are slow, and their profiles show `COVERAGE_STATS_OPTIMIZER`: cost-based optimizer statistics are missing, so the plan uses standard heuristics. The same queries on managed tables in the catalog never show this insight, and a manual OPTIMIZE last month did not change it. The analyst wants better plans without changing who writes the table or how. Which action fits?

choices.text: Enable automatic liquid clustering with CLUSTER BY AUTO on the table, since automatic clustering also collects optimizer statistics
Schedule ANALYZE TABLE ... COMPUTE STATISTICS FOR ALL COLUMNS after loads, since predictive optimization maintains only managed tables
Enable predictive optimization explicitly on the table with ALTER TABLE, since the account setting is inherited only by new tables
Schedule OPTIMIZE on the table after loads, since compacting files also collects the optimizer statistics that the plan is missing

stem: A partner-facing AI/BI dashboard is shared with registered account users who are not members of any workspace. It is published with individual data permissions, and the partners hold SELECT and the usage privileges on all tables it uses. Three widgets show data for them, but two widgets stay empty, while employees in the workspace see all five. The empty widgets read `partner_ops.metrics.sla_daily`; the others read tables in `shared_ops`. A workspace admin mentions that `partner_ops` was bound to the company workspace for an audit last month, and the contract says partners must never become workspace members. Which change makes the two widgets work for the partners?

choices.text: Republish the dashboard with shared data permissions, so that the two widgets run with the publisher's credentials against the bound catalog
Grant the partners BROWSE on partner_ops in addition to SELECT, so that account users can resolve tables inside workspace-bound catalogs
Remove the workspace binding from partner_ops, or move sla_daily to a catalog that is not workspace-bound, keeping the partners' grants as they are
Add the partners to the workspace with the Consumer access entitlement only, so that they still cannot open the draft or edit any dashboard

stem: A Lakeflow pipeline finishes refreshing `sales.gold.daily_kpis` at 06:10. The dashboard on it is published with shared data permissions and has a schedule at 05:30 that refreshes data without subscribers. At 08:00, managers still see yesterday's numbers, and the analyst sees no new query on the warehouse in query history since 05:30, although dozens of managers opened the dashboard. A colleague reruns a dataset query in the SQL editor at 08:05 and gets today's figures. The pipeline team suggests adding a step to its pipeline that refreshes the table again at 07:00. What should the analyst do?

choices.text: Ask the pipeline team to add the 07:00 table refresh, because a change to the underlying data invalidates the dashboard cache automatically
Republish the dashboard with individual data permissions, because the per-user cache is rebuilt whenever the source table is updated
Keep the schedule and set the warehouse auto stop to a longer value, because the stopped warehouse is what makes the cache serve old data
Move the dashboard schedule to after 06:10, or add a dashboard task after the pipeline in a job, because only that refreshes the dashboard cache

stem: An alert should fire when any of the last seven days had more than 500 failed payments. Its query is `SELECT day, count(*) AS failed FROM pay.events WHERE status = 'FAILED' AND day >= current_date() - 6 GROUP BY day ORDER BY day ASC`, and the condition is set to the first value of `failed` greater than 500. On Thursday, the result shows 812 failures for Tuesday, yet the alert history records OK for Thursday's evaluation. Monday, the oldest day in the window, had 120. No evaluations were skipped, and the on-call team wants a single row-independent condition. Which change makes the alert fire correctly?

choices.text: Set the condition to the MAX aggregation of the failed column greater than 500, so the check covers every row instead of the first one
Keep the first-value condition and turn on Notify on OK, so the team also hears about days when the first row stays below the limit
Set the condition to the SUM aggregation of the failed column greater than 500, so the check covers every row instead of the first one
Keep the first-value condition and sort the query by day DESC, so the first row checked is the newest day of the seven-day window

stem: A Genie Agent for regional sales uses `sales.gold.orders`, which has a Unity Catalog row filter so that each manager sees only their own region, and `sales.ref.states`, a small lookup table without filters. Users asking "orders in Florida last month" get empty answers because the generated SQL filters `state ILIKE '%Florida%'`, while `orders.state` stores codes such as `FL`. The curator tries to turn on entity matching for `orders.state`, and the agent does not allow it. The row filter must stay, and the curator cannot change the gold tables but may add sources to the agent. Which change lets Genie map state names to codes?

choices.text: Enable entity matching on the state column of a dynamic view over orders, because a dynamic view applies its own logic instead of the row filter
Enable entity matching on orders.state after adding a column mask, because a column mask replaces the row filter for prompt matching purposes
Enable entity matching on orders.state after hiding all other columns, because the row filter excludes only the columns the filter function reads
Enable entity matching on the full state name column of sales.ref.states and define the join to orders, because the row filter excludes orders

stem: A curator built benchmarks for a Genie Agent from real conversations. Most pass, but three always fail in Chat mode: "And how does that compare with last year?", "Now break it down by channel" and "Same for EMEA". Each has a SQL Answer that matches the intended result, written for the question that came before it in the original chat. In those chats Genie answered correctly, and the agent's instructions and example queries have not changed. The curator wants the benchmark score to reflect real accuracy. What explains the failures, and what should the curator change?

choices.text: Benchmarks run inside one shared conversation in list order, so switch the run to Agent mode, which keeps the thread across the questions
Benchmarks run as new conversations without thread context, so rewrite each as a self-contained question that names the measure and period
Benchmarks run inside one shared conversation in list order, so move the three follow-up questions directly after the questions they extend
Benchmarks run as new conversations without thread context, so add the earlier questions to the same benchmark set right before them

stem: A support portal embeds a Genie Agent in an iframe generated from the agent's Share dialog. A workspace admin added the portal's domain to the allowed embedding surfaces, the agent author has CAN MANAGE, and support staff, who hold CAN RUN and SELECT on the data, sign in when prompted and get correct answers. However, the Copy CSV action and the copy conversation link action do nothing inside the portal, while both work when the same users open the agent directly in Databricks. The portal team pasted the iframe code with only `src`, `width` and `height`. What fixes it?

choices.text: Add the portal domain to the allowed embedding surfaces again, which the embedded agent needs for copying CSV data and links
Grant the support staff CAN EDIT on the agent, which the embedded agent needs for copying CSV data and conversation links
Add allow="clipboard-write" to the iframe element, which the embedded agent needs for copying CSV data and conversation links
Add allow="clipboard-read" to the iframe element, which the embedded agent needs for copying CSV data and conversation links

stem: In an AI/BI dashboard the author models `orders` (fact), `customers`, `regions` and `countries` with dashboard relationships: orders to customers (many-to-one), orders to regions (many-to-one), customers to countries (many-to-one) and regions to countries (many-to-one). A chart of revenue by country now fails with an ambiguous join path error, although each relationship has the right key and cardinality and charts by customer or by region work. The business uses two meanings: the customer's billing country and the country of the sales region, and the CFO wants both available as separate fields. Which change resolves the error?

choices.text: Alias countries once per route, such as Country (customer) and Country (region), so each path from orders leads to its own copy
Change the orders to customers relationship to many-to-many, so that the engine can choose the route to countries at query time
Pre-join customers and regions in the orders dataset SQL, so that countries can be joined once to the combined dataset by one key
Remove the relationship from regions to countries, so that orders reaches countries through customers only and the path is unique

stem: A dynamic view masks salaries: `CREATE VIEW hr.secure.v_staff AS SELECT name, CASE WHEN is_member('hr_auditors') THEN salary ELSE NULL END AS salary FROM hr.core.staff`. The group `hr_auditors` was created by the identity team in the account console and assigned to the workspace, and Maria is a confirmed member. On a SQL warehouse she sees NULL salaries, while a colleague in an old workspace-local group named `hr_auditors` sees real values. Unity Catalog grants on the view are identical for both. The rule is that only members of the account group may see salaries. Which change fixes the view?

choices.text: Keep is_member('hr_auditors') and add Maria to the old workspace-local group as well, so that the existing check also finds her membership
Replace is_member('hr_auditors') with is_account_group_member('hr_auditors') in the CASE expression, because this function evaluates account-level group membership
Replace is_member('hr_auditors') with is_member('account:hr_auditors') in the CASE expression, because this form evaluates account-level group membership
Replace is_member('hr_auditors') with current_user() = 'hr_auditors' in the CASE expression, because this test evaluates account-level group membership
